text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The Danish government is to look into the sale of 48 percent of J.Lauritzen's Danyard shipyard to Malaysia's Penang Shipbuilding Construction SDN BHD (PSC) following defence ministry contentions that the deal involves the sale of modern warship technology contrary to Danish law. The yard itself insists that the deal only involves hull construction knowhow but foreign minister Niels Helveg Petersen wants the prime and justice minister to investigate the matter.

--Denmark is isolated on the issue of the Schengen open-borders accord after outsiders Britain and Ireland said they would not take action to hinder other European Union member states from further developing the arrangement. Denmark, which has opt-outs on the Maastricht Treaty's joint EU cross border policing and asylum policies, had called for a slowing of efforts to intensify Schengen cooperation and hoped that London would support it.
--Many small companies in Denmark risk chaos and financial ruin because their computer systems will not be able to cope with the millenium problem in the switch from the year 1999 to 2000.

--Confusion about the outlook for East Asiatic (EAC) could make attract major speculation in the share on the stock exchange this summer following unclear announcements about its first half and whole year 1997 expectations. The wholesale and graphic group recently downwardly adjusted expectations for the first six months of 1997 but the management denied that this implied any downgrading for the whole year.
